name: Ibnijah
overview: Ibnijah was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, noted specifically as such in 1 Chronicles 9:8. His identity is primarily established by his tribal affiliation as a Benjaminite. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ibnijah means 'y-h-v-h built,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's role in his existence. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8 and was not given directly by God but holds a meaningful connection to divine providence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Ibnijah was the son of Reuel, as inferred from 1 Chronicles 9:8. He is explicitly identified as a descendant of Benjamin, linking him to the patriarch of the tribe. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ibnijah's significance lies in his representation of the faithful lineage within the tribe of Benjamin after the exile. His mention in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 9:8 underscores the continued preservation of Israel's tribal heritage and God's faithfulness in maintaining His people. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the importance of genealogical continuity in God's redemptive plan.
